alignments.note: Construct noun; the determiner belongs to the possessor's word (rule 29).
Rectum rendered as an English possessive, taking the determiner standing before its own word at the phrase's left edge (rule 29).
Prepositional predicate of a verbless clause takes the construction-supplied copula, headed on the preposition (rule 49).
Noun with its own indefinite article (rule 15).

Articleless attributive participle recast as a relative clause: the supplied relative stays with the attributive (rule 41), and the light verb plus complement heads on the complement (rule 44). The margin's *doeth shamefully* was read and set aside (rule 38).

Anarthrous participle substantive with the supplied *him that* (rule 46); the supplied *against* states what this bare nominal contributes to the clause and belongs to it (rule 33), never the head, and the light verb plus complement heads on the complement (rule 44). The ASV italic on *against* corroborates that no preposition morpheme stands there (rule 7).
